- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- Model consistently underestimates sharp upward moves (spikes) in true outcomes; add lagged momentum adjustment to forecast.
- After a spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope after peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — over-predicts decline after recent rise; adjust for recent trend persistence.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent underestimation of true price peaks; increase baseline by 2–5% if sentiment is positive or volatility is rising.
- If sentiment is negative or flat, model tends to underestimate true price; apply upward bias correction.
- Model fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment >0.2, increase forecast variance or add stochastic adjustment.
